mainTopic: Whether temporarily unusable food stays מוקצה, and whether a בכור's blemish may be checked on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof about מוקצה. Beans and lentils are edible, become inedible while cooking, and are edible again once done. אביי rejects the proof, because by that logic every pot still boiling at בין השמשות would be forbidden. So the גמרא narrows the question to things finished by heaven, like figs and grapes drying in the sun, and that question stays unresolved. Next comes a story: רבי יהודה נשיאה sent a בכור to be checked for a blemish on יום טוב, and the hesitating sages were told the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון. רבי אבא objects, citing רבי זירא for רבי שמעון. רבי זירא himself says he only said רבי שמעון's view 'makes sense'. רב יוסף then brings an ancient tradition from the holy community in ירושלים that ties not checking a בכור on יום טוב to רבי מאיר's view in בכורות. אביי rejects that link: רבי מאיר's ruling there is only a קנס, and רב נחמן בר יצחק confirms this from the wording of the משנה. The amud ends with אמי ורדינאה, who would not check firstborns on יום טוב, and רבי אמי's approval of him. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finished cooking makes the food fit again
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי זירא's proof: beans and lentils become edible again once their cooking is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: When their cooking is finished, they are fit to eat again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started on the previous amud. Beans and lentils are fit, then become unfit while cooking, then become fit again when they finish cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether food that was usable, became unusable, and then became usable again stays forbidden as מוקצה. Beans in the pot fit that pattern, and everyone agrees we eat them afterward. So the proof claims that temporary unfitness does not make food forbidden for the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: They are fit (for use or eating)
Set aside; an item not usable on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: When their cooking is finished, they are fit for them (to eat).
phrases.notes: Last stage of the beans-and-lentils proof: fit, then unfit, then fit again.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר בִּשּׁוּלַיְיהוּ חֲזוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That food which was temporarily unfit does not stay מוקצה once it becomes fit again.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The everyday case of beans and lentils being cooked on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי: ordinary boiling pots would be a problem too
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Under that reasoning, every pot still boiling at בין השמשות would be forbidden, yet we eat from it that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: By your reasoning, ordinary pots should be a problem for you. Ordinary pots are usually still boiling at בין השמשות, and yet we eat from them in the evening!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. He points out that if cooking food counted as 'unfit', every Friday-night pot would become forbidden, which is clearly not the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food that is still cooking at the key moment of בין השמשות would count as unfit by this logic. Since everyone eats it at night, this kind of 'unfitness' was never real מוקצה at all. So cooking food cannot prove anything about the real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the start of שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to your reasoning, ordinary pots should be a difficulty for you,
for ordinary pots in general
are boiling at twilight,
and in the evening we eat from them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וּלְטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from beans and lentils.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Food still being cooked was never truly מוקצה; otherwise ordinary שבת pots would be forbidden. So it cannot prove anything about the real question.

steps.title: The question is narrowed to things finished by heaven
steps.stepSummary: Food that a person finishes is clearly allowed. The open question is only about items that finish naturally, like drying figs and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, about something whose completion is by human hands, we have no question. Our question is about something whose completion is by the hands of heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא redefines what the question really is. Cooking is no longer part of the question; only naturally finished items remain in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food a person is actively cooking is understood as 'ready' in that person's mind, so it is not set aside. Figs and grapes drying on the roof depend on the sun, so a person may truly put them out of mind while they are unfit. That case stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Its completion is by human hands
Its completion is by heaven (naturally, e.g., drying in the sun)
We have a question about it

steps.whatToRemember: No one doubts that food a person is cooking stays permitted. The open question about מוקצה is only for things finished naturally, like figs and grapes drying, and it stays unresolved.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not answer the original question. It only narrows it, and the narrowed question stays open.

phrases.english: Rather, something whose completion is by human hands
we have no question about.
Where we have a question
is something whose completion is by the hands of heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּמָרוֹ בִּידֵי אָדָם לָא קָא מִבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's point and redefines the scope of the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Things a person finishes are not מוקצה; the doubt applies only to things heaven finishes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה's firstborn sent to רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי hesitated to check a בכור on יום טוב and was told that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה had a firstborn animal. He sent it to רבי אמי, who thought he should not examine it. רבי זריקא, and some say רבי ירמיה, said to him: In a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of checking a בכור for a blemish on יום טוב, and tells a story. A sage hesitated to check it, and a colleague reminded him of the rule for deciding the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה lets an expert check a בכור on יום טוב to see if it has a blemish that permits it. רבי שמעון says a blemish not known before יום טוב makes the animal מוקצה. רבי אמי leaned toward caution, but the general rule favors רבי יהודה, so checking is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animal (בכור), which may only be eaten once it has a blemish
And some say (a different name for the speaker)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first position in the debate: checking a בכור on יום טוב is allowed, following רבי יהודה. רבי אבא challenges it in step 6, רב יוסף brings a tradition the other way in step 13, and רבי אמי praises not examining on יום טוב in step 22.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בּוּכְרָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia had a certain firstborn animal.
He sent it before Rabbi Ami,
who thought not to examine it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika, and some say Rabbi Yirmeya, said to him:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon:
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בּוּכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מוקצה question and returns to the משנה about checking a בכור on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so the בכור may be checked on יום טוב.

steps.title: Sent again to רבי יצחק נפחא, same rule
steps.stepSummary: The scene repeats with רבי יצחק נפחא, who also hesitated and was given the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then sent it before רבי יצחק נפחא, who thought he should not examine it. רבי ירמיה, and some say רבי זריקא, said to him: In a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The same thing happens a second time with a different sage. Again a colleague reminds him that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition shows that both great sages hesitated about checking a בכור on יום טוב. Each time, the clear rule of deciding like רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון settled it. Notice that the two names are given in reverse order this time.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: He then sent it before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
who thought not to examine it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי זְרִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya, and some say Rabbi Zerika, said to him:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon:
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story with a second sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Again: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so the בכור may be checked.

steps.title: רבי אבא objects to the ruling against רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges the one who ruled like רבי יהודה: why did you stop the rabbis from acting like רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: Why did you not let the rabbis act according to רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא questions the ruling from the previous steps. He wants to know why the rabbis were not allowed to follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 4-5, the rabbis were told the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. רבי אבא's question implies he thinks רבי שמעון is the accepted view, so the earlier ruling looks wrong to him.

keyTerms.meaning: you let them / you allowed them
to act in practice (to make a practical ruling)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
phrases.notes: Spoken to the one who told the rabbis to follow רבי יהודה (Sefaria identifies him as רבי ירמיה).

phrases.english: What is the reason you did not allow the rabbis
to act in practice according to Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא שְׁבַקְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling given to רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי שמעון is the accepted view, it was wrong to stop the rabbis from following him.

steps.title: What is your source?
steps.stepSummary: The one who ruled asks רבי אבא what tradition he has for following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And you, what do you have in hand?
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering, the one being challenged asks back: what source do you have? This sets up רבי אבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A practical ruling needs a source. He is asking whether רבי אבא has a real tradition that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: What do you have in your hand? (What tradition do you hold?)

phrases.english: He said to him: And you, what do you have in hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אבא's challenge by asking for his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What tradition supports ruling like רבי שמעון?
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאַתְּ מָה בִּידָךְ

steps.title: רבי אבא cites רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that רבי זירא said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי זירא said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives his source: a ruling he heard in the name of רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two rulings in conflict: one for רבי יהודה and one, quoted from רבי זירא, for רבי שמעון. The next steps check whether the quote from רבי זירא is accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who moved from Bavel to ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Zeira said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זירא ruled that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא

steps.title: A traveler asks רבי זירא directly
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed person hopes to go to ארץ ישראל and hear the ruling from רבי זירא himself. When he arrives, he asks whether רבי זירא really said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain person said: May I merit to go up there and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master. When he went up, he found רבי זירא and asked him: Did the master say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone wants to check the quote at its source, so he travels and asks רבי זירא directly. This sets up רבי זירא's clarification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quotes passed from person to person can change slightly. Going to the original speaker is the surest way to know exactly what was said.

keyTerms.meaning: may I merit and go up (to ארץ ישראל)
from the mouth of its master (the one who said it)

phrases.english: A certain person said:
May I merit to go up there,
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל, where רבי זירא lived.

phrases.english: and learn the teaching from the mouth of its master.
When he went up there,
he found Rabbi Zeira and said to him:
Did the master say the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר מַאן דְּהוּא: אֶזְכֵּי וְאֶסַּק לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks whether רבי אבא's quote of רבי זירא is accurate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי זירא actually rule that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?

steps.title: רבי זירא: I only said it makes sense
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא denies giving a firm ruling. He only said that רבי שמעון's view 'makes sense'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. I said 'it makes sense'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא corrects the quote. He never said 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון'; he only said it seemed logical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הלכה' is a firm ruling to act on, while 'מסתברא' is only a reasoned opinion. So the quote that רבי אבא relied on was stronger than what רבי זירא actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense / it is reasonable

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'הלכה כ...' (a binding ruling) with 'מסתברא כ...' (only a reasoned leaning). The whole story depends on this difference.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
I said: "it makes sense."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, אֲנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא אֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the traveler and weakens רבי אבא's source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the wording of the quote, not the leaning toward רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי זירא's 'it makes sense' was passed on as a firm 'the הלכה is'.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון's view makes sense
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains his reasoning: רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה is taught in a ברייתא in the name of the חכמים, so it is reasonable to follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches: רבי שמעון says any בכור whose blemish was not visible while it was still day is not 'prepared', and a ברייתא teaches the same thing in the name of the חכמים, learn from this that it makes sense to follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shows the basis for his 'it makes sense'. The same rule that the משנה gives in רבי שמעון's name appears in a ברייתא as the view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows the majority (חכמים). If a ברייתא presents רבי שמעון's rule as the view of the חכמים, that suggests many held it. That is a good reason to lean his way, but it is not a received ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: while it is still day (before יום טוב began)
among the things prepared for use on יום טוב
in the name of the Sages (the majority)

phrases.english: Since it teaches in our Mishnah:
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם —
phrases.english: Any [firstborn] whose blemish was not visible while it was still day
is not among the things prepared [for יום טוב],
and a baraita teaches it in the name of the Sages —
learn from this that it makes sense [to rule] like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי זירא's 'מסתברא'.
steps.raayaObject: That ruling like רבי שמעון is reasonable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that teaches רבי שמעון's rule in the name of the חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא never gave a firm ruling. He only leaned toward רבי שמעון because a ברייתא presents his rule as the view of the חכמים.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion is on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back and forth, the גמרא asks for the bottom line. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have one ruling for רבי יהודה and only a 'makes sense' for רבי שמעון. The גמרא wants a decisive answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the final ruling after the conflicting reports.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view does the הלכה follow in checking a בכור on יום טוב?

steps.title: רב יוסף: a tradition from 'great trees' rules like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a long chain of tradition, going back to the holy community in ירושלים, that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear, for this hangs on great trees. רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, in the name of רבי, in the name of the holy community in ירושלים: רבי שמעון and his colleagues said the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers with an old, highly respected tradition. It says the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Hangs on great trees' means the question was settled by very great early sages. The long chain of names shows how strong the tradition is. The גמרא will next explain how רבי מאיר's view connects to the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the start of the final answer. Instead of a 'makes sense' opinion, we now have a strong received tradition.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear,
for it hangs on great trees.
For Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that Rabbi said in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:
Rabbi Shimon and his colleagues said
phrases.notes: Per Sefaria, this is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, not the רבי שמעון of our משנה.

phrases.english: the halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַלְיָא בְּאַשְׁלֵי רַבְרְבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the final ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ancient tradition says the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'רבי שמעון' in this tradition is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, not the רבי שמעון whose view is being argued about in our משנה.

steps.title: How could older sages 'say' a ruling like a younger sage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יוסף's tradition. The elders of ירושלים are much older than רבי מאיר, so why would they report the הלכה as following him?
steps.simpleTranslation: They 'said' it? But they are much older than him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the tradition from the last step. It seems strange that older sages would rule 'like' a younger sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the הלכה follows רבי מאיר' suggests the speakers lived after him and chose his view. But the sages of the קהלא קדישא דבירושלים were much older than רבי מאיר. So the wording of the report can't be understood literally.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely, but isn't it so (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: They 'said'?!
phrases.notes: Picks up the last word of רב יוסף's report and questions it.

phrases.english: But they are much older than him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִינְהוּ קַשִּׁישֵׁי מִנֵּיהּ טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב יוסף's chain of tradition from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that the elders 'said' the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Older sages would not rule by following a younger sage, so the report can't be read literally.

steps.title: They ruled according to רבי מאיר's approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the tradition. The elders did not pick רבי מאיר's ruling. Their own position simply matches רבי מאיר's way of thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they said it in line with the approach of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The elders' ruling (no checking a בכור's blemishes on יום טוב) fits רבי מאיר's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Following רבי מאיר' does not mean the elders came after him. It means their ruling grows out of the same idea that רבי מאיר holds elsewhere. This sets up the need to show where רבי מאיר holds that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: in line with the approach of

phrases.english: Rather: they said it according to the approach of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲמָרוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the tradition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The elders chose רבי מאיר's ruling as the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The elders' ruling matches רבי מאיר's approach, which they shared.

steps.title: The source: רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה in בכורות where רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its blemish. From this it infers that he holds a בכור must be examined while alive, unlike a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone slaughtered a בכור and only afterward showed its blemish to an expert, רבי יהודה permits it. רבי מאיר says that since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden. So רבי מאיר holds that checking a בכור is not like checking a טרפה. A בכור is checked while alive, but a טרפה is checked after slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי מאיר's approach comes from. In the בכור case, he says the animal must be checked by an expert before it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking whether an animal is a טרפה can be done after slaughter, because it is just finding out facts. Checking a בכור's blemish must happen while the animal is alive, so according to רבי מאיר it is a stricter, more formal process. That is why a בכור shown to an expert only after slaughter is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
firstborn animal; may only be slaughtered and eaten if an expert confirms a permanent blemish
an expert who rules on blemishes
an animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: One who slaughters a firstborn
and afterward showed its blemish (to an expert)
Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
And Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden.
Apparently Rabbi Meir holds:
examining a firstborn is not like examining a tereifa;
examining a firstborn is done while it is alive,
examining a tereifa is done after slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶרְאָה אֶת מוּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for 'רבי מאיר's approach' mentioned in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר treats checking a בכור as a stricter process than checking a טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורות (28a): רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered before an expert examined it.

steps.title: So a בכור must be checked before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: From רבי מאיר's view, the elders concluded that checking a טרפה is allowed on יום טוב, but checking a בכור must be done on ערב יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this we learn: checking a טרפה may be done even on יום טוב, but checking a בכור must be done before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the practical rule about יום טוב from רבי מאיר's view. This explains the elders' ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking a טרפה only finds out facts, so it is fine on יום טוב. Checking a בכור is a stricter, formal process, a bit like giving a judgment. So it must be finished before יום טוב, which is the ruling of the קהלא קדישא דבירושלים.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִינַּהּ: רְאִיַּית טְרֵפָה — אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And from this: examining a tereifa may be done even on Yom Tov,
examining a firstborn must be done from the eve of Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ: רְאִיַּית טְרֵפָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 16 to the question of יום טוב.
steps.raayaObject: The elders' ruling that a בכור's blemish may not be checked on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's distinction between checking a בכור and checking a טרפה (step 16).
steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading, the ruling of the קהלא קדישא דבירושלים rests on רבי מאיר's idea that checking a בכור is a formal process done while the animal is alive. That makes it unfit for יום טוב, unlike checking a טרפה.

steps.title: אביי: their dispute is about a penalty, not about examining
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר in that משנה are not arguing about how blemishes are examined. They are arguing about a penalty (קנס).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him (רב יוסף): Do they really argue there about examining blemishes? They argue about a penalty!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the proof from the בכורות משנה. He says it has nothing to do with how a בכור must be examined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, רבי מאיר forbids the animal only as a penalty, because the owner slaughtered without asking an expert first. He does not hold that a בכור's examination must be done while alive. So nothing can be learned from him about examining blemishes on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: is it so that...? (rhetorical, introduces a rejection)
a penalty imposed by the רבנן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר holds the meat is truly forbidden by its nature. According to אביי, it is forbidden only as a punishment for skipping the expert.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (Rav Yosef):
Is it so that there they disagree about examining blemishes?
They disagree about a penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ הָתָם, בְּרוֹאִין מוּמִין פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the בכורות משנה used in steps 16 and 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רבי מאיר treats checking a בכור as an examination that must be done while alive.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's dispute is about penalizing someone who acted improperly, not about how the examination works.

steps.title: Proof from blemishes in the eyelids
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his view with רבי יוחנן's statement. For eyelid blemishes, everyone agrees the slaughtered animal is forbidden, because such blemishes change after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: with blemishes in the eyelids, everyone agrees it is forbidden, because they change.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source to show that the real dispute is about a penalty. Only for blemishes that change after death does everyone forbid the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eyelid blemishes look different after death, so an expert cannot judge them properly afterward. That is a real reason to forbid, and everyone agrees. This implies that for blemishes that don't change, רבי יהודה permits, and רבי מאיר forbids only as a penalty, not because the check must be done while the animal is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: the eyelids / membranes of the eye

steps.whyThisMatters: This takes away the support for the elders' ruling coming from רבי מאיר. The גמרא will now need to look at the question of checking blemishes on יום טוב differently.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
With blemishes in the eyelids,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden,
because they change.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the support for אביי's claim in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That the בכורות dispute is about a penalty and not about how the examination works.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן: for eyelid blemishes everyone forbids, because they change after death. So in other cases the dispute must be about a penalty.

steps.title: The real dispute is about body blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The statement of רבי יוחנן that אביי cites continues. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about blemishes on the body. רבי מאיר forbids them as a גזירה because of eye blemishes, and רבי יהודה does not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is about blemishes on the body. רבי מאיר holds that we make a decree forbidding body blemishes because of eye blemishes. רבי יהודה holds that we do not make such a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The quote from רבי יוחנן, which אביי brought as support, finishes by telling us exactly what רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eye blemishes change after death, so everyone agrees an animal slaughtered with one is forbidden. Body blemishes (like a cut ear) do not change, so an expert could still judge them after slaughter. רבי מאיר forbids them anyway, so people won't mix them up with eye blemishes. רבי יהודה does not make that decree. This means the dispute is about a protective decree, not about whether a בכור must be checked while alive.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a rabbinic decree (a protective rule)
Blemishes on the body, which look the same after death
Blemishes in the eye, which change after death
Because of, on account of (the reason behind a decree)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר holds that body blemishes really can't be judged after death. He agrees they can. He forbids them only as an extra protective decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This takes away the elders' proof from step 17. If רבי מאיר's ruling is only a decree, it says nothing about whether a בכור must be examined while alive.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about blemishes on the body,
Rabbi Meir holds:

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרִינַן מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף אַטּוּ מוּמִין שֶׁבָּעַיִן.
phrases.english: We decree against body blemishes because of eye blemishes.
phrases.notes: If people were allowed to slaughter first with body blemishes, they might do the same with eye blemishes.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: we do not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּמוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 19. Step 19 said everyone agrees about eye blemishes. This step says where they actually argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids a בכור with a body blemish slaughtered before an expert saw it, as a גזירה because of eye blemishes. רבי יהודה does not make that גזירה.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה shows it is a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points to רבי מאיר's words, 'since it was slaughtered without an expert.' Those words sound like a penalty, which supports אביי. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The משנה is also precise this way. It says, 'רבי מאיר says: since it was slaughtered without an expert, it is forbidden.' Learn from this that he is imposing a penalty. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings proof for אביי from the exact wording of the משנה, and the גמרא agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not say 'because the blemish can't be checked after death.' He says 'since it was slaughtered without an expert.' That reason is about what the person did wrong, so it sounds like a penalty for acting without permission. The final 'שמע מינה' means the גמרא accepts the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise; the wording supports this reading
An expert authorized to judge blemishes
A penalty or fine imposed by the Rabbis
Learn from this; said a second time, it confirms the proof

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי מאיר's ban is a קנס for slaughtering without an expert. It is not a rule that a בכור must be checked while alive. So the elders' יום טוב distinction cannot be proven from רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the challenge to the elders' proof. It confirms that רבי מאיר's ruling is about penalty, not about how blemishes are examined.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The mishna is also precise this way,
for it teaches: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The reason given is about acting without an expert, not about checking the blemish.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: קְנָסָא הוּא דְּקָא קָנֵיס,
phrases.english: Learn from this: it is a penalty that he imposes,
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's reading in steps 18 and 20 with the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר's ban is a קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה in בכורות: 'since it was slaughtered without an expert'

steps.title: אמי ורדינאה did not examine firstborns on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אמי ורדינאה examined firstborns for the household of the נשיא but would not do so on יום טוב. רבי אמי said he was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמי ורדינאה was the examiner of firstborns in the household of the נשיא. On יום טוב he would not examine them. People came and told רבי אמי. He said to them: He is doing well by not examining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a real examiner who would not check a בכור's blemish on יום טוב, and רבי אמי approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Examining a blemish on יום טוב is like making a legal ruling, which may be forbidden on יום טוב. רבי אמי's approval suggests that checking a בכור should not be done on יום טוב. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אַמֵּי וַרְדִּינָאָה חָזֵי בּוּכְרָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Ami of Vardina was the examiner of firstborns for the household of the Nasi.
On a Festival he would not examine.
They came and told Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: שַׁפִּיר קָא עָבֵיד דְּלָא חָזֵי.
phrases.english: He said to them: He does well not to examine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּי וַרְדִּינָאָה חָזֵי בּוּכְרָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section with a story about examining a בכור on יום טוב, the topic the elders raised in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי approved of not examining a בכור's blemish on יום טוב.

steps.title: But רבי אמי himself examined firstborns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אמי could praise not examining on יום טוב, since he himself examined firstborns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אמי himself would examine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. רבי אמי praised not examining, yet he himself examined firstborns on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reports about רבי אמי seem to clash. He praised אמי ורדינאה for not examining, but he was known to examine himself. The גמרא must explain how both are true.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Ami himself examine!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי גּוּפֵיהּ חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's approval in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's statement that not examining on יום טוב is proper
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי's own behavior seems to contradict his praise.

steps.title: רבי אמי examined on the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when רבי אמי examined, he did it on ערב יום טוב, not on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אמי examined, he would examine from the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי examined the blemishes on ערב יום טוב, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי did his examining on the day before יום טוב, to see whether the blemish was permanent. Because the main examination was done before יום טוב, his practice is different from examining on יום טוב itself. The sentence continues on the next amud, which explains how this fits his approval of אמי ורדינאה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the day before (ערב יום טוב)

phrases.english: When Rabbi Ami would examine,
he would examine from the day before,
phrases.notes: The thought continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי חָזֵי מֵאֶתְמוֹל הֲוָה חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case (timing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי examined firstborns on יום טוב itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי did his examining on ערב יום טוב, so his behavior matches his ruling.
